tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot. Add PerLinearFt=per_linear_ft (+ label), wire LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType->lf, seed a per-LF trim LaborRate. Must land before takeoff pricing.

prep.understand: `RateType` drives `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()`, which maps each rate type to a unit string (`sf`, `ea`, etc.). There is no `lf` unit today — any linear-foot measurement creates a broken line item with no unit. You also need a seeded `LaborRate` row so the takeoff seeder can look up a trim rate by the new type.

tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. Add a wall/ceiling height input (project default + optional per-room override); wall paint SF/room = perimeter x height. The seeder currently DROPS geometry — preserve it.

Three-part fix: (1) add `wall_height_ft` (default 9 ft) to the project + optional per-room override, (2) stop the seeder from discarding `perimeter`, and (3) derive `wall_paint_sf = perimeter × height` and emit it as a named measurement kind for t46 to route.

Find the geometry-drop point in `TakeoffEstimateSeeder` and preserve `perimeter` through the import pipeline.
Write `deriveWallPaintArea(room, projectHeightFt)` → `perimeter × height` (no door/window subtractions for v1).
Emit the result as a `wall_paint_sf` measurement kind on each room and verify it appears in the seeder output.

prep.what: Rewrite the seeder to switch on measurement kind and emit trade-tagged line items — replacing the single anonymous `kind=custom` line with real flooring / paint / trim / door entries.

tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)

prep.what: Build the PG-backed durable job queue the Sweeper (t21) will consume — lease/heartbeat/reclaim so jobs survive restarts and can't double-run.
prep.understand: The queue needs at-least-once delivery: a worker atomically claims a job (writes `worker_id` + `leased_until`), heartbeats while running, and a daemon reclaim pass resets stale leases back to `pending`. It must also enforce the active window (don't dequeue outside the 5h work window), cap concurrent workers, and respect priority. Postgres + `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` is the right primitive — no Redis, no external services. The Sweeper (t21) will be the first consumer.
approach: Write `enqueue(kind, payload, priority, runAt?)` and `dequeue(workerId, windowStart, windowEnd, maxConcurrent)` using `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for atomic single-flight claim.
Write `heartbeat(jobId, workerId)` (extends `leased_until`) and `reclaimStale(timeoutMs)` (resets timed-out running jobs to pending up to `maxRetries`).

Write tests: enqueue → dequeue → done; heartbeat keeps lease alive; reclaimStale fires after simulated timeout; window gate: job not dequeued outside active hours; cap: no more than N concurrent workers.
